Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) may have a potential role in differentiating between unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS) and minimally conscious state (MCS) patients.

For UWS patients who lack purposeful behavior due to motor-output failure, tDCS could be useful in identifying residual connectivity markers. Research suggests that fMRI displays a high concordance with the further clinical course of patients in an VS who showed significant activation of ROIs (Regional Involvement). Therefore, proposed the term "functional minimally conscious state" for these patients.

On the other hand, tDCS may not be as effective in differentiating MCS patients from those who lack consciousness. Patients in a MCS may also show signs of functional remission or improvement on fMRI, which may not be apparent with tDCS alone.

It is essential to note that further research is needed to confirm this hypothesis and determine the optimal application of tDCS for differentiating between these two conditions.
